properties.state: {"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"Drift rolls up to one number, and how far the work retreats is computed from it","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"reflow2 records drift per event and never rolls it up, so there is no answer to \"how bad is it overall, and how far back do we have to go?\" DriftEvent carries severity (low/medium/high/critical) and drift_type (missing_artifact, spec_mismatch, undocumented_addition, status_mismatch, checksum_change, and the three deployment_* kinds), and 37 of them exist in reflow2's own design — but nothing aggregates them into a single figure and nothing acts on the aggregate. THE PRIOR ART, from reflow's resync_protocol.json and phase_transitions.json: drift detection emitted a scalar drift_score in 0.0..1.0, and that one number decided HOW FAR THE WORK RETREATED — below 0.3 return to P3 and keep building, 0.3 to 0.5 return to P2 and revise the allocation, at or above 0.5 return to P1 and revise the functional analysis. The same number gated the forward transition too: P4 to P5 required \"architecture drift score < threshold\" among its quality gates, and major_drift (> 0.5) was classified severity critical with escalates_to P1. So one measure served three purposes — trigger, escalation target, and release gate. A PRECONDITION THAT MUST BE FIXED FIRST, and it is why this is not a small feature: the per-event input is currently untrustworthy. The 2026-07-28 sweep behind req:defaults-do-not-assert recorded DriftEvent.severity among the properties WRITTEN and never consulted — \"written from kind.severity() at three call sites while ranking independently re-derives it via severity_rank(kind), so the stored copy can silently diverge from the mapping that actually governs.\" A rollup over a stored value that the ranking already disagrees with would compute a confident number from an inconsistent base. Either the stored severity becomes the single source or the rollup reads the derivation, but not both. OPEN, and deliberately not decided here: whether the retreat target should be phase-shaped at all. reflow's answer was P3/P2/P1 because it had phases; reflow2's equivalent question is which LAYER of the golden thread a given drift score sends you back to — realization, allocation, or intent. The scalar is portable; the destinations are not. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows. Anthony's word: capture it.","status":"proposed"}
